requested.title: Server-only `.server.svelte` component is compiled into the browser bundle when Bun's runtime resolver and the bundler resolver disagree
`scanComponentExports` warnings are computed and then discarded, so unstubbed `export *` in a `.server.svelte` module script is silent
Reserved `__mochi_ah` envelope key is not shadowed on the pure `mochi:defer` path, letting a user-controlled prop key force sealed server-island props to be echoed back in plaintext
A nested `mochi:*` directive inside a `mochi:defer` / `mochi:clientOnly` child fragment throws a raw MagicString error instead of a framework compile error
`buildPropsFromAst` interpolates attribute names as bare object keys, so a hyphenated prop on any island emits invalid JavaScript
`css-bundle-failed` compile errors are never cleared by `compileAll` and are re-pushed on every rebuild, leaving every page permanently 500-ing in dev
`registerEsmEnvStrip`'s filter hard-codes POSIX separators, so dev-only Svelte code is never eliminated from client bundles built on Windows
`IDENT_RE` admits reserved words, so a reserved-word export name generates `export const class = …` and fails the whole client build

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: I verified every link in the chain. serverOnlyComponents.ts:34 classifies a specifier as relative only for `./`, `../` or absolute; everything else goes to `Bun.resolveSync` (L42) and a throw returns `undefined` (L43), handing the specifier back to Bun's default resolution — and the existing test at serverOnlyComponents.test.ts:112 shows that fall-through is deliberate. I then confirmed nothing else claims such a module: the sibling `.server.ts` onResolve filter is `/\.server(?:\.[jt]s)?$/`, which cannot match a string ending in `.svelte`; `serverOnlyModuleGuard`'s `CANDIDATE_SPECIFIER` only matches extensions/mochiConfig/requestContext/env; and `registerServerOnlyComponentStubs`'s onLoad is namespace-scoped. So the file lands in the default `file` namespace and is claimed by the generic `/\.svelte$/` onLoad at ComponentRegistry.ts:1380, which runs `backend.compile(..., { generate: 'client' })` — a server-only component compiled into a publicly served island bundle, silently. The asymmetry the finding highlights is real: the `.server.ts` resolver (L1346-1361) always returns the stub namespace and never falls through. On the trigger, I split the two claims. The tsconfig-`paths` claim is the weaker one: Bun's bundler and `Bun.resolveSync` share the same resolver and the same enclosing-tsconfig discovery (docs: /docs/runtime/module-resolution 'Path re-mapping'), so I would not expect them to diverge on `$lib/*`. The export-conditions claim, however, is architecturally certain: the client build passes `conditions: ['svelte', 'production'|'development']` and `target: 'browser'` (L1424-1425) while `Bun.resolveSync(moduleId, parent)` has no conditions parameter and runs the default runtime condition set. This is not theoretical — `node_modules/@lucide/svelte` in this very repo exposes `"./icons": { "types": ..., "svelte": ... }` with no `default` key, i.e. a subpath that only resolves when the `svelte` condition is supplied. A Mochi-targeting component library packaged the same way and shipping a `Foo.server.svelte` is exactly the fail-open case. Reachability is therefore narrow (it needs a third-party package using Mochi's own `.server.svelte` convention behind a condition-gated export), and the impact is attenuated because many real `.server.svelte` files import `node:`/`bun:` and would fail the browser build loudly (that is what the `ssr-only-barrel` integration test asserts via `readFileSync`). But a component whose server-ness is only markup, an internal URL, or a prerendered literal would ship silently. I keep MEDIUM: a security control that fails open with information-exposure impact, low likelihood, and a trivially safe fix (return the stub namespace on resolve failure, plus a belt-and-braces throw in the generic `.svelte` onLoad for paths ending `.server.svelte`).

Confirmed by direct reading of both halves of the mechanism. `scanComponentExports` (serverOnlyComponents.ts:17-30) returns `{ ...scan, hasDefault: true }`, so `scan.warnings` produced by `scanServerOnlyExports` flows out intact; the consuming onLoad at L50-57 passes the whole object into `buildServerOnlyStubModule` and never touches `.warnings`, and there is no logger imported into the file at all. The `.server.ts` twin does log them — ComponentRegistry.ts:1365-1367 iterates `scan.warnings` through `logger.warn` — so the two arms of one mechanism genuinely behave differently. I also confirmed both warning sources are reachable for a `.server.svelte`: serverOnlyScan.ts:32 pushes the `export *` warning from the sliced `<script module>` source, and serverOnlyScan.ts:22 pushes the string-named-export warning, which serverOnlyScan.test.ts:158-165 proves `Bun.Transpiler.scan()` actually surfaces (`export { x as "weird-name" }` → warning). The parse-failure fallback at L29 does hard-code `warnings: []`, so the same information is dropped there too. Consequence is exactly as stated: a missing stub export surfaces as Bun's opaque "No matching export" build failure, or as a silent `undefined` for a namespace import, with the explanatory diagnostic discarded. Not a security issue — a developer-experience/observability bug — so BUG is the right severity.

Both ends verified against current HEAD. Producer: svelteAstPreprocess.ts:295 emits `__mochi_ah` in `autoEntries` only when `directives.hydrate` is set, and L313's envelope appends `, __mochi_ah: ...` only under the same condition — so on a pure `mochi:defer` the key is omitted rather than pinned, and whatever `...__mochi_props__` contributes for it survives into the sealed envelope. The reserved-name guard at L216-223 rejects only a literal `islandId` attribute and cannot see spread keys at all. Consumer: Mochi.ts:1591-1593 destructures the mode straight out of the decrypted payload and `isAlsoHydrateMode` accepts it; Mochi.ts:1656-1668 then `devalueStringify(props)` and emits `props="..."` into the returned HTML whenever the mode is non-null. I checked for a secondary guard and there is none: `getComponentEntryUrl` returning undefined only omits `component-url`, the `props=` attribute is still written, and the mode also flips `isHydratable()` context on at L1627. This breaks a guarantee the docs state verbatim — packages/docs/70-server-islands.md: 'A pure `mochi:defer` island keeps its props on the server — the token on the wire is opaque and the endpoint returns only HTML. ... Do not pass server-only secrets to an island you also hydrate.' It also violates the module's own stated invariant: `buildPropsFromAst`'s doc comment (L529-531) says `extraEntries` are 'framework-owned keys appended last so they win over a user spread', which is precisely what does not happen for `__mochi_ah` here. Concrete attack: a page renders `<Widget mochi:defer {...Object.fromEntries(url.searchParams)} apiToken={secret} />`; the attacker requests `?__mochi_ah=eager`, the envelope seals with the mode inside, the browser's ServerIsland fetch of `/_mochi/island/:name` returns the whole props bag — including `apiToken` — as plaintext devalue in a `props` attribute. Exploitation needs the app to spread untrusted keys into a pure-defer island that also carries server-held props, so likelihood is modest, but the control is defeated and the fix (pin `ALSO_HYDRATE_ENVELOPE_KEY: null` unconditionally on both paths) is one line. MEDIUM retained.

I traced this to the MagicString source rather than trusting the claim. node_modules/magic-string/dist/index.mjs: `update()` calls `_split(start)` then `_split(end)` (L1051-1052) before applying the edit, and `_splitChunk` throws `MagicStringError('cannot split a chunk that has already been edited ...')` when `chunk.edited && chunk.content.length` (L1294-1297). After the parent's `s.overwrite(comp.start, comp.end, replacement)`, exactly one chunk spans that range and it is edited with non-empty content. A nested child Component's `start` lies strictly inside that range, so `byStart`/`byEnd` miss, `_chunkAt`/`_split` walk to the edited chunk (`contains(child.start)` is true because `comp.start <= child.start < comp.end`), and `_splitChunk` throws. I also confirmed the walk reaches the child: `next()` is called at L433 after both the clientOnly overwrite (L260) and the server overwrite (L347), and zimmerframe's `next()` descends into `comp.fragment.nodes`, where the `Component` visitor fires again. The plain-`mochi:hydrate` branch is immune because `hasRealChildren` pushes a `hydrate-children` error and returns before any overwrite (L351-356), but `mochi:defer` and `mochi:clientOnly` treat children as fallback, so the nesting is reachable there. Nothing catches it: `cachedPreprocessHydratable` has no try/catch, so the throw escapes the `.svelte` onLoad and compileAll surfaces it as `Svelte SSR build failed: ... cannot split a chunk that has already been edited`, bypassing the `PreprocessIslandError` channel whose doc comment (L36-41) explains island problems are pushed to `errors` rather than thrown. The comment at L232-233 asserts nested islands 'stay untransformed', which is not what happens, and svelteAstPreprocess.test.ts has no directive-carrying-child case (only plain `<div>` children and the hydrate-children error path), so the behaviour was assumed, never verified. Diagnostics-quality bug, not security: BUG is correct.

Verified line by line. All four `entries.push` sites in `buildPropsFromAst` (L544, L547, L556, L571) splice `attr.name` in as a bare object key, and the only name filter is `attr.name.startsWith('mochi:')` (L540). For `data-testid="row-1"` the value is a single Text part, so the pure-text branch emits `data-testid: "row-1"`, producing the object literal `{data-testid: "row-1"}` — which JS parses as `data - testid`, a syntax error. That text is spliced into a Svelte expression tag (`props-ref={__mochi_emit_props__(...)}` at L382/L240, or the signed-props envelope at L300/L318), so the Svelte compiler reports a parse error in framework-generated source the author never wrote. Two independent confirmations that the preconditions hold: (a) Svelte's AST keeps arbitrary attribute names as plain `Attribute` nodes — `findMochiDirectives` relies on exactly that to see `mochi:hydrate`, whose name is not an identifier either; (b) dashed attributes on components are legal and already idiomatic in this repo — `aria-hidden="true"` is passed to `@lucide/svelte` components in packages/docs/_components/Callout.svelte:16, ComparisonTable.svelte, PersistenceTable.svelte, packages/site/src/ci/*.svelte. Those call sites are not islands, which is exactly why the bug is latent: `buildPropsFromAst` never runs on them. I confirmed the inner component invocation is unaffected (`propsSource` at L363-366 re-emits raw attribute source), so only the serialized props payload breaks. svelteAstPreprocess.test.ts covers literals, entities, nested braces, `<` in expressions and arrow functions, but no non-identifier attribute name. Given how common `aria-*`/`data-*` forwarding is, a user is fairly likely to hit this. Correctness/DX bug, no security impact: BUG.

Both halves confirmed. I enumerated every mutation of `this.errors` in ComponentRegistry.ts: the reconciliation filter at L929-934 drops only `nested-hydration`, `defer-in-hydratable`, `unresolved-island`, `server-only-island` and `hydrate-island-children`; L2390 drops only `font-subset-invalid`; `css-bundle-failed` is pushed from seven sites (L2207, 2214, 2239, 2259, 2296, 2314, 2327) and cleared from exactly one, L2501 inside `rebundleImportedCss`. I then checked the callers: `rebundleImportedCss` is reached only from devWatcher.ts:262 via `triggerCssReload`, which devWatcher.ts:765 gates on `filePath.endsWith('.css')`; `clearCompileCache()` (which would reset `errors` at L2106) has no callers anywhere in src. And Mochi.ts:898-901 throws `MochiHttpError(500, formatCompileErrors(...))` for every page render whenever `getErrors()` is non-empty. So a single `css-bundle-failed` entry 500s the whole app until a `.css` file is touched or the process restarts — even after the real cause is fixed. The duplicate-accumulation half is also right, and I found it splits cleanly by sub-path: the two early-return failures (L2207, L2214) never reach `importedCssUrls.set(variant, urlPath)` at L2347, so `todo`'s `!this.importedCssUrls.has(variant)` filter at L2178 re-attempts them on every forced `compileAll` and pushes an identical entry each time (the `.css` onLoad at L787 fires even on a compile-cache hit, so `importedCssPaths.size > 0` and L1232-1233 runs). The font-subset catch at L2292-2297 does not early-return, so that variant *is* registered and instead yields a single error that persists forever — and because the variant key is derived from `hash(groups)` at L2446 while the error is keyed on the bare `cssPath`, fixing the offending import attribute in a `.ts`/`.svelte` file creates a new clean variant while the stale error lingers. cssImports.test.ts:145 asserts one error after one compile but never tests clearing or repeat compiles, so the gap is untested. Dev-experience bug, not security: BUG.

The filter `/node_modules\/svelte\/src\/.*\.js$/` (clientBuildLoaders.ts:29) is unambiguously separator-dependent, and I confirmed it is load-bearing: node_modules/svelte/package.json maps `.` to `./src/index-client.js` (so Svelte really resolves under `node_modules/svelte/src/`), 49 files under svelte/src import from `esm-env`, and esm-env's exports resolve `DEV` through the `production`/`development` conditions — so without the strip, `DEV`/`BROWSER`/`NODE` stay imported bindings and Bun's `define` map in `clientBuildDefine()` (L17-24) cannot substitute them, exactly as the comment at L26-27 describes. I also confirmed this is the only Bun plugin filter in the repo that embeds a directory path: every other one (`IMAGE_FILE_FILTER`, `PRERENDER_MODULE_FILTER`, `MARKDOWN_FILE_FILTER`, `/\.svelte$/`, `/\.css$/`, the specifier-anchored ones) is extension- or specifier-only, and it is the only one that cannot be normalized inside the handler because the match happens inside Bun. The premise that Bun hands onLoad a native, backslash-separated path on Windows is strongly supported but is the one link I could not prove statically (I did not run code): the repo itself treats plugin `args.path` as native in two independent places — ComponentRegistry.ts:848 uses `${path.sep}node_modules${path.sep}` and prerenderModules.ts:30/42 normalize with `toPosixPath()` before testing `/node_modules/` — Bun's own changelog states the Windows separator 'may either be `\` or `/`' (v1.1.21 coverage fix) and that `bun build` on Windows wrote backslash-separated asset paths (v1.4.1), and `[\\/]` is the established esbuild-plugin convention for exactly this reason. No test exercises the strip (virtualModuleTemplate.test.ts's probe never imports svelte), so CI gives no signal either way. Impact is bundle size and platform-dependent output, not behaviour or security — values stay correct at runtime — so BUG, and the fix (`/node_modules[\\/]svelte[\\/]src[\\/].*\.js$/`) is risk-free.

Mechanically correct. `IDENT_RE = /^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/` (serverOnlyScan.ts:7) matches reserved words, and an ESM `ExportSpecifier` accepts any `IdentifierName`, so `export { del as delete }` / `export { Row as class }` is valid source and importable as `import { class as X }`. The scan at L16-23 therefore routes such a name into `named` rather than the warning branch, `buildServerOnlyStubModule` emits `export const ${name} = ...` (L54), and `safeName` (L47) resolves to the reserved word itself because `IDENT_RE.test` passed, yielding `function class() {}` (L49). Both positions require a binding identifier, where reserved words are illegal, so the synthetic stub module is a hard SyntaxError — and because onLoad contents are parsed as part of the graph, the whole island client build fails pointing at a module the developer never wrote. I corroborated that `Bun.Transpiler.scan()` reports alias names verbatim (not normalized or dropped) via serverOnlyScan.test.ts:158-165, where `export { x as "weird-name" }` surfaces as the name `weird-name`; a reserved-word alias is reported the same way but, unlike the string form, passes `IDENT_RE` and so is not caught. The repo already knows the safe pattern — prerenderModules.ts:182 uses the indirect `export { local as name }` form, where any `IdentifierName` is legal. Likelihood is low: aliasing an export to a reserved word is awkward to consume and nobody in this repo does it, and strict-mode-reserved words like `package`/`private` can only arrive via such an alias. So it is a genuine but unlikely codegen robustness gap, correctly scoped as BUG, and the recommended indirect-export fix would additionally let the currently-dropped string-named exports be stubbed properly.
